title: Catching a wave: Long Lake Expansion announcement ‘a sign of more to come’
summary: With network expansion capacity, Enbridge looks to ‘capture our share’ of Canadian oil sands production growth
body_markdown:
With network expansion capacity, Enbridge looks to ‘capture our share’ of Canadian oil sands production growth


November 23, 2026


Far from the beaches of Oahu, Malibu and the Gold Coast, Enbridge is ready to catch another wave.


That wave being another surge in Canadian oil sands production.


Industry forecasts expect Western Canada Sedimentary Basin supply **[to grow by as much as 1 million barrels per day by 2035](https://www.enbridge.com/~/media/Enb/Documents/Investor-Relations/2026/Q3_2026_Earnings_Presentation_Final.pdf)** , surpassing the 5MMbpd mark.


So Enbridge’s Nov. 6 announcement of **[our C$200M Long Lake Expansion project](https://www.enbridge.com/media-center/news/details?id=123894&lang=en)** , supporting CNOOC Petroleum North America’s growing operations in northern Alberta, could very well be the beginning of a long-range expansion of our well-established Athabasca liquids pipelines system.

“There's a **[huge wave of production coming up in Alberta](https://www.enbridge.com/~/media/Enb/Documents/Investor-Relations/2026/2026_Q3_Transcript.pdf#page=22)** that we need to get to the Edmonton and Hardisty hubs. We have some pre-built capacity there,” noted Colin Gruending, Enbridge’s Executive Vice President, and President of our Liquids Pipelines group, on Nov. 6 during our Q3 financials earnings call.


“I think we're on the cusp of a huge cyclical and hopefully sustaining growth wave up there . . . we've got a strong position in the oil sands region. Seven trunklines, lots of laterals, lots of customers,” added Mr. Gruending.


**TOP AND ABOVE PHOTOS** : Enbridge moves about 70% of U.S.-bound Canadian oil exports, largely in part to our Athabasca pipeline system, which has a takeaway capacity of about 2.5 million barrels per day.


“There's a lot of operating leverage in these systems. They're pre-built. There's some headroom in them. And I think a number of the bigger customers are in the midst of a big negotiation. So, I think it's a sign of more to come and we'll certainly look to capture our share.”


Per our Nov. 6 announcement, Enbridge has sanctioned the Long Lake Expansion project, strengthening connectivity to CNOOC Petroleum North America’s Long Lake oil sands asset, with a new lateral pipeline and storage tank alongside capacity expansion on our Waupisoo (Line 18) and Wood Buffalo Extension (Line 45) pipelines.

Currently, **[Enbridge’s Athabasca pipeline system](https://www.enbridge.com/~/media/Enb/Documents/Reports/2026-LP-Customer-Handbook/2026_LPCH_ENB_ROS_system_configuration.pdf)** has a takeaway capacity of about 2.5 MMbpd through four trunk lines traveling from the Fort McMurray region to either our Edmonton Terminal or Hardisty Terminal:


- The **[Waupisoo Pipeline](https://www.enbridge.com/map?#map:infrastructure,search=waupisoo%2018)** , a.k.a. Line 18 (580,000 bpd).
- The **[Woodland/Woodland Extension Pipelines](https://www.enbridge.com/map?#map:infrastructure,search=woodland%2049/70)** , a.k.a. Lines 49/70 (540,000 bpd, expandable to 800,000 bpd).
- The **[Athabasca Pipeline](https://www.enbridge.com/map?#map:infrastructure,search=athabasca%2019)** , a.k.a. Line 19 (570,000 bpd).
- The **[Athabasca Twin Pipeline](https://www.enbridge.com/map?#map:infrastructure,search=athabasca%20twin%2045)** , a.k.a. Line 45 (800,000 bpd).


“We’re well aware of the various competing, bigger greenfield ideas. And so, we will continue to offer up kind of a series of expansions,” said Mr. Gruending.


“We have this incumbency and we’re going to play to those strengths, whether it’s on the Mainline path with its seven pipelines or the Express path, which is, as a reminder, has a Presidential permit for larger volume.”
